parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Detailed Meanings

😎
adjoining[ad3dinin]adj.
If something is adjoining, it is next to or joined with a building, or room.
→ I couldn’t sleep because the people in the adjoining room were loud.
😎
allege[aied3]v.
To allege something is to say that it is true without offering proof.
→ The little girl had alleged that her older brother hid her favorite doll.
😎
arch[a:rtj]n.
An arch is a curved opening formed under a structure such as a bridge or doorway.
→ The arch of the bridge was not high enough for the tall boat to pass underneath.
😎
assemble[asembal]v.
To assemble means to get together in one place.
→ The parents assembled to discuss ways to improve their children’s education.
😎
casualty[kse3ualti]n.
A casualty is a person killed or injured in a war or an accident.
→ The only casualty in the car accident was a woman who broke her arm.
😎
erect[irekt]v.
To erect something means to build it.
→ The king erected two towers on the north and south sides of his castle.
😎
foul[faul]adj.
If something is foul, then it is not pleasant or enjoyable.
→ He wouldn’t let his dog drink from the water because it had a foul smell.
😎
hectare[hektear]n.
A hectare is a unit of measure equal to 10,000 square meters.
→ His family farm covered many hectares.
😎
heighten[tiaitn]v.
To heighten an emotion means to increase the intensity of it.
→ The pleasant music heightened their enjoyment of the wonderful dinner.
😎
hospitality[haspitselati]n.
Hospitality is friendly behavior and entertainment given to guests or strangers.
→ The travelers were amazed at the hospitality given them by the hotel’s staff.
😎
mansion[msenjen]n.
A mansion is a large and expensive home.
→ The mansion had thirty bedrooms, two kitchens, and a pool.
😎
outnumber[autnAmba/-]v.
To outnumber a group means to have a greater number than it.
→ The girls outnumbered the boys at the school by four to one.
😎
overjoyed[ouvard3oid]adj.
If someone is overjoyed, then they are extremely happy.
→ He was overjoyed by the news of his promotion.
😎
pasture[psestjar]n.
A pasture is an area of land covered with grass for animals to use as food.
→ The sheep were taken to a pasture where there was more grass.
😎
petition[pitijan]n.
A petition is a written request asking an authority to do something.
→ The citizens all signed a petition asking the mayor to repair the sidewalks.
😎
renovate[renaveit]v.
To renovate a building means to repair it or build new structures on it.
→ The old fire station was renovated into an apartment building.
😎
revise[rivaiz]v.
To revise something means to change or update it to make it better.
→ When the editor discovered certain facts were wrong, he revised the book.
😎
slab[slaeb]n.
A slab is a large, thick, flat piece of stone, concrete, metal, or wood.
→ I looked at various slabs of stone to decorate my house.
😎
terrace[teras]n.
A terrace is an open area that is connected to a house or an apartment.
→ In the afternoons, she liked to sit on the terrace and check her email.
😎
turf[ta:rf]n.
Turf is a section of grass and the dirt in which it grows.
→ After the game, the turf looked ragged.

sections.title: Exercise 3: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: Once the weather was renovated, the day was warm and sunny. Now, we were all able to go on a picnic in the park.
questions.explanation: Renovate applies to buildings, not weather.

questions.content: The scientists worked all day in the slab. They were inventing a new plastic that would not melt under the extreme heat of the sun.
questions.explanation: Slab is a piece of stone, not a laboratory.

questions.content: The amount of cows outnumbered the pigs. There were more pigs than cows.
questions.explanation: Contradictory sentence.

questions.content: Why don’t you connect those two large blue arches, so that you can form a giant square?
questions.explanation: Arches are curved, not straight to form a square.

questions.content: The worse casualty from the earthquake was a woman who broke a leg.
questions.explanation: Casualty refers to injured people.

questions.content: The two enemies erected a wall between their properties. They had hoped that it would reduce any future arguments.
questions.explanation: Erected means built.

questions.content: Whenever Doug was in a foul mood, everyone enjoyed being around him.
questions.explanation: Contradictory sentence.

questions.content: The glass was filled with a hectare of water.
questions.explanation: Hectare measures land area, not volume of water.

questions.content: This is the kitchen, and the adjoining room is the dining room.
questions.explanation: Adjoining means next to.

questions.content: The visit lacked in hospitality. There was nothing to eat and nowhere to sit.
questions.explanation: Hospitality means friendly behavior and entertainment.

questions.content: You can stay in the house tonight, but your dog has to sleep outside in the mansion.
questions.explanation: Mansion is a large expensive home, not a dog house.

questions.content: William alleged all the way home. As a result, he was out of breath and sweaty by the time he got there.
questions.explanation: Allege means to accuse, not to run or exert physically.

questions.content: The grandmother was overjoyed to see her grandchildren. She couldn’t stop smiling when she saw their lovely faces.
questions.explanation: Overjoyed means extremely happy.

questions.content: This room here is the pasture. It’s where we keep all our old furniture.
questions.explanation: Pasture is a field for animals, not a storage room.

questions.content: The manager read his employees’ petition. They wanted a longer lunch break.
questions.explanation: Petition is a written request.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Lord and the Farmers

A wealthy lord was renovating his mansion. He had added another story to his home with large windows that overlooked the farmers’ pastures on the eastern border of his land. Around the mansion, he then erected a great wall. He built an arch for the gate out of huge slabs of stone. The lord was overjoyed with the addition to his home.

However, one day while he was sitting on the terrace, some farmers knocked at his door. He invited them in. Despite his hospitality, the farmers appeared to be in a foul mood.

“Why are you so upset?” the lord asked.

One farmer replied, “That is actually the reason for our visit.” He then handed the lord a petition. It alleged that the shadow cast by the mansion was harming their pastures. “Your mansion now casts a shadow over several hectares of our land,” the farmer explained. “The turf in the shadow has died, and our cattle now have less grass to eat.”

“It is too late for me to revise my plans,” the lord answered. “You will just have to live with the change.”

His reply only heightened the farmers’ anger. They left, but they assembled that night outside the mansion’s gate. They planned to destroy the mansion. The lord’s servants tried to defend the house, but the farmers outnumbered them.

The servants fled, and the farmers rushed into the mansion and set it on fire. Everyone got out of the house, and there were no casualties. However, the fire soon spread from the house to the adjoining pastures that belonged to the farmers.

Both sides’ properties were destroyed. The lord and the farmers were sorry for their actions. The lord promised to pay for the burned pastures, and the farmers promised to rebuild the mansion. They had learned that when you fight, both sides lose.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: The farmers that assembled outnumbered the lord’s servants.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Ở cuối đoạn 6 có viết: "The lord’s servants tried to defend the house, but the farmers outnumbered them." (Những người hầu của lãnh chúa cố gắng bảo vệ ngôi nhà, nhưng những người nông dân đã áp đảo họ về số lượng).

questions.content: Despite the lord’s hospitality, the farmers appeared to be overjoyed.
questions.explanation: Câu này SAI. Trong đoạn 2 viết: "Despite his hospitality, the farmers appeared to be in a foul mood." (Mặc dù ông đã tiếp đón họ rất nồng hậu, nhưng những người nông dân có vẻ đang trong tâm trạng rất tồi tệ). Từ "foul mood" (tâm trạng tồi tệ) trái ngược với "overjoyed" (vui mừng khôn xiết).

questions.content: The lord built an arch for the gate out of slabs of stone.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Đoạn 1 có miêu tả: "He built an arch for the gate out of huge slabs of stone." (Ông ta đã xây một vòm cổng từ những phiến đá khổng lồ).

questions.content: When the lord said it was too late to revise his plans, it heightened the farmers’ foul mood.
questions.explanation: Câu này ĐÚNG. Ở đoạn 6 ghi rõ: "His reply only heightened the farmers’ anger." (Câu trả lời của ông ta chỉ làm cơn tức giận của những người nông dân tăng thêm).

questions.content: The pastures were owned by the lord.
questions.explanation: Câu này SAI. Trong truyện viết (đoạn 1 và 4) rằng đồng cỏ thuộc về những người nông dân: "...overlooked the farmers’ pastures..." (nhìn xuống những đồng cỏ của những người nông dân) và "...our cattle now have less grass to eat." (...gia súc của chúng tôi hiện có ít cỏ hơn để ăn).

questions.content: What did the farmers’ petition allege?
options: It alleged that the shadow cast by the mansion was harming their pastures.
It alleged that the lord stole their cows.
It alleged that the lord erected a great wall.
It alleged that the lord poisoned the water.
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 4, khi đưa lá đơn kiến nghị, người nông dân nói: "It alleged that the shadow cast by the mansion was harming their pastures." (Lá đơn cáo buộc rằng cái bóng do dinh thự đổ xuống đang làm hỏng đồng cỏ của họ). Do đó đáp án A là đúng.

questions.content: While renovating, what did the lord erect around his mansion?
questions.explanation: Trong đoạn 1 có viết: "Around the mansion, he then erected a great wall." (Sau đó, xung quanh dinh thự, ông ta đã dựng lên một bức tường lớn). Đáp án A là chính xác.

questions.content: What happened to the pastures adjoining the burning mansion?
options: The pastures adjoining the burning mansion also burned.
questions.explanation: Cuối đoạn 7 có viết: "However, the fire soon spread from the house to the adjoining pastures that belonged to the farmers." (Tuy nhiên, ngọn lửa đã nhanh chóng lan từ ngôi nhà sang những đồng cỏ liền kề thuộc về những người nông dân). Vậy nên đồng cỏ cũng bị cháy, đáp án A đúng.

questions.content: Why were there no casualties in the fire at the mansion?
options: There were no casualties in the fire at the mansion because everyone got out of the house.
They sued him for the loss of their pastures.
Because the fire was very small.
questions.explanation: Ở đoạn 7 có ghi: "Everyone got out of the house, and there were no casualties." (Mọi người đều đã thoát ra khỏi nhà, và không có thương vong nào). Đáp án A là câu trả lời chính xác.

questions.content: While he was sitting on the terrace, who knocked on the mansion door?
options: While he was sitting on the terrace, some farmers knocked at his door.
questions.explanation: Ngay câu đầu của đoạn 2 có viết: "However, one day while he was sitting on the terrace, some farmers knocked at his door." (Tuy nhiên, một ngày nọ khi ông đang ngồi trên sân thượng, một số nông dân đã gõ cửa nhà ông). Do đó đáp án A đúng.
